entry.title: a small guide to immutability
entry.content:
I spent a while getting immutability wrong. Here is the version that works for me.

why it matters

Immutability shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: what i learned about immutability
entry.content:
A quick write-up on immutability, mostly so future me stops relearning it.

why it matters

Immutability shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: thinking about immutability
entry.content:
Short post: immutability is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Immutability shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
